studies.name: Open almanac
studies.structure: An unboxed continuous editorial spread: prose, large facts, flowing columns and marginal personal annotations share a single reading canvas. Avoid a two-column hero followed by numbered sections. Native vertical reading with an editorial contents index; wide type/columns collapse into a deliberately re-composed linear phone essay. No card slabs.

studies.name: Rival halves
studies.structure: A true split-screen confrontation: own team and opponent each own one half, with a central scoring seam and synchronized comparative reading. Team facts, players and saved choice align across the seam. League-wide views replace the comparison with an explicitly different full-width reader. Phone gives a legible two-sided score then side tabs, preserving context. Not one matchup hero above a normal dashboard.

studies.name: Query commons
studies.structure: A search-first homepage made of a giant usable query field and an open typographic action index, then direct mixed team/player/action results in the same canvas. Empty search already has useful current facts and concrete task paths. Selecting a result expands an inline contextual answer; search is local, no AI or provider. Mobile keeps query/results at the center. Distinct from task-rail workspace: no persistent sidebar or pane grid.

studies.structure: A folding atlas of full-width, unequal-height chapter spines. Opening a spine unfolds a large integrated spread in-place and collapses the prior spread, with visible contextual neighbours. This is navigation through an accordion book, not ten independent rounded cards. Default chapter is useful; keyboard/Escape/back restore. Phone retains strong spine shapes with a single readable unfolded chapter.

studies.method: Actual initial-load records plus browser state API; grayscale reduced-motion; all advertised states in public/member desktop1440 andphone390. Real viewport plus whole document. No position/CSS flattening. Scrollable interior content needs its own views and explicit pane checks; these images are structural evidence, not final complete-content acceptance.

studies.name: Parallel dispatch
studies.structure: Four unequal vertical running channels, each a continuous unboxed thread (your team, league action, scouting, culture), with independent reading positions on desktop. Cross-links deliberately relate items across channels. Phone selects a channel with a visible all-channel index and remembers position. Avoid small bordered cards or a fixed central focus pane; the simultaneous parallel streams are the architecture.

studies.method: Actual initial-load records plus browser state API; grayscale reduced-motion; all advertised states in public/member desktop1440 andphone390. Real viewport plus whole document. studies.name: Black-line ledger
studies.structure: A ledger-first, whole-page working data sheet: team and matchup rows, meaningful aligned columns, expandable inline subrows for rosters/personal evidence/editorial. No hero and no cards. Category index and sort/filter operate on the sheet itself. Desktop dense but readable; phone changes to labelled row records with a persistent column/field chooser. Distinguish nulls/zero and keep narrative source reading comfortable.

studies.name: Franchise yearbook
studies.structure: An alphabetic and numeric franchise field guide: a large open directory built from hanging team names, staggered approved portrait cutouts and precise locator marks. A–Z/rank index and roster search are primary; activating a franchise inserts a full-width in-flow dossier that pushes the index apart. Personal bookmark jumps to your actual franchise. No equal-card gallery, no sidebar workspace, no conventional hero.
